newsitem.title: UK: Airfreight role for new UK distribution centre.
newsitem.headline: Airfreight role for new UK distribution centre.

text.p: Airfreight will be an important component of a planned multi-modal cargo distribution centre at Alconbury Airfield, near Huntingdon, central England the local authority said.

"Multi-million pound" investment in the project will be required, addeds Kingspark Developments Ltd, one of two companies which will be participating with the landowner, the Ministry of Defence, in the proposed development of the former 1,022-acre RAF Alconbury site.
Kingspark and Lynton Plc are forming a joint company, Alconbury Developments Ltd, to develop, promote and market the airfield, 19 miles northwest of Cambridge.
They plan to lease the land from the ministry, which will be an active partner in the new consortium, said the estate agency acting on the ministry's behalf, Bidwells.

Future air cargo use of RAF Alconbury, a former U.S. air force base, is the most controversial issue in terms of impact on the surrounding area of the proposed freight centre, said Huntingdonshire District Council planning department's Richard Probyn.

"It is the aspect of the project that must be looked at most carefully. We are concerned at just how the airfield will be used in future, what the aircraft types will be, possible requests for overnight flights and the overall impact on the community," he told Reuters.
Bidwells said the early stages of the development will include facilities for road freight users and construction of a railfreight terminal will be a priority.

Colin Beasley, Kingspark's commercial director, said that road services would be followed by railfreight services, with the potential for airfreight use coming later. He added that no figure could be put on the investment required as this depended on the size and scope of the eventual project and demand requirements from interested users.
Probyn said that "a big investment will be needed" to upgrade the airfield which has a 2,750-metre runway able to take Boeing 747s.
A planning application is due to be submitted by the developers this summer. Probyn felt that a public consultation process could take a year before any approvals were given.
